sessionReview.title: Old KING Forged · club first test
sessionReview.cue: All irons: old KING Forged / KBS 120 stiff. Your feel: get the club started down and through first. 4i and 7i have separate before/after blocks; no KING TECs today.
sessionReview.takeaway: The cue produced mixed results: 7i carried farther with a tighter kept-shot carry spread, but its path moved farther left. 4i lost carry. No overall cue or shaft verdict yet.
sessionReview.story:
4i — SAME OLD CLUB, BEFORE → CLUB FIRST: 160.0 → 148.7 yd carry (14/15 → 18/21 clean); best five 169.3 → 156.6. Speed 81.5 → 78.5 mph, ball speed 115.2 → 109.2; smash 1.414 → 1.392. Path -7.9° → -6.3° is somewhat less left, but face-to-path stays open (+6.5° → +6.1°). The after-cue path mean includes a retained +6.6° shot; medians -8.4° → -7.0° still point left. Carry SD tightened 9.1 → 7.0 yd at a lower distance. This does not show a 4i comeback or a reason to unbench the KING TEC 4i, which was not used.

7i — SAME OLD CLUB, BEFORE → CLUB FIRST: 122.5 → 136.1 yd carry (+13.6); 5/7 → 5/8 clean. Ball speed 94.7 → 100.3, smash 1.268 → 1.312, apex 50 → 72 ft; carry SD 7.6 → 4.0. There is a real observed speed/flight gain among kept shots, but not a directional fix: path -2.1° → -5.6°, face-to-path +0.5° → +5.5°. Absolute face-to-path grew 1.3° → 5.5° too, so the small pre-cue mean is not just positive and negative values cancelling. Retention fell from 5/7 to 5/8; five good shots are not the whole consistency story. More leftward path and more open face-to-path are compatible with a stronger cut tendency for centered right-handed strikes, but curve/finish was not measured numerically.

OLD SET VS KING TEC: Your feeling is useful, but there was no KING TEC trial today. The old 4i pre-cue 160.0 is only +3.2 yd versus the Sep 25 KING TEC same-rule 156.8; the old after-cue 4i is lower. Today's old 7i after-cue 136.1 is -12.2 yd versus Oct 1 KING TEC 148.3, with club speed 76.4 versus 79.8 mph. Different dates, effort, heads, lofts and conditions prevent a shaft-flex/weight conclusion. Old 6i before cue: 142.3 carry, best five 148.7, 8/10 clean; no today post-cue 6i comparison.

5W: 192.3 carry; best five 193.1; 6/11 clean across two separately preserved blocks. Compared with Nov 11 3H: carry 190.4 → 192.3; apex 62 → 72 ft; face-to-path +2.8° → +5.0°. Similar distance with a higher measured peak; more open-to-path delivery and no landing-angle measurement. The late jump in the mixed table is the club change to 5W, not a 4i breakthrough.

NEXT TEST: Test one question at a time. First, old 7i with usual feel versus club first, alternating short blocks at the same target and normal effort; record every attempt. Compare kept fraction, carry, path and absolute face-to-path. Then test old versus KING TEC with the same cue, ball and target, and match speed ranges. Record actual loft/shaft specs. Down-the-line and face-on film can test sequencing; radar tables cannot. Keep the 4i benched and playing distances as saved.

briefing.focus: Current feel: CLUB FIRST — get the club started down and through first. All November 14 irons were old KING Forged / KBS 120 stiff, not KING TEC. Same-club 4i/7i before-and-after results are mixed; sequencing was not filmed.

sections.k: Your late-session cue · old KING Forged irons
sections.b: YOURS: get the club started down and through first in the downswing. This is a feel, not an instruction to flip the clubhead past the hands or stop body rotation. Today, old 4i carry 160.0 → 148.7; old 7i 122.5 → 136.1. The 7i flight gain came with a more leftward path and more open face-to-path. Retest without stacking more swing thoughts; use footage to evaluate movement.

YOURS, and it is four months old before anyone wrote it down: the shaft is a Project X LZ 5.5 in REGULAR, in since June. On the old stiff shaft you hit a consistent cut that ran to a slice. On this one you are about 15 yards longer with much less curve — a straight ball that can miss BOTH ways. That is your read, not a measurement: no launch data exists on either shaft.

[STANDARD] Why a shaft does that, because it decides what to do next. A shaft too stiff for your load will not let the tip deflect and close, so the face arrives open to the path — a cut, plus low dynamic loft, which is where the 15 yards were sitting. A softer tip lets the face square. The cost is that a face which CAN square can also over-square, and that is your two-way miss. The miss is the receipt for the distance.

WHAT IT DID NOT DO is fix your path. Flex governs how the FACE arrives, not where the club TRAVELS — so the over-the-top, out-to-in path is still an open fault, untouched and still unmeasured. Read the straight ball as a path fault being CANCELLED by a face change, not as a path that got better. One useful thing follows: your path is already fade-shaped, so a fade is a shape you own rather than one you have to manufacture.

THE PLAY, unchanged: aim the CENTER of the fairway and swing LONGER, not tighter. [STANDARD] Aiming away from a known miss is textbook, not something you worked out. What HAS changed is the old rule that the bad one is the push-slice — with this shaft the bad one goes either way, so centre-aim is doing more work than it used to.

If you want the one-way miss back, the lever is the sliding weight on the sole and NOT the loft. The Aug 31 section of the Workshop Log has the reasoning; the short version is that toe weight bends the curve without moving your start line, and lowering the loft moves both.
sections.k: Regular shaft since June: ~15 yds longer, much less curve — but the miss now goes BOTH ways, and your path is unchanged.

sections.t: Putting — it lives in the Putting lab
sections.b:
This section used to carry a putting key, and it went stale the moment the putter changed — it still said 'hands EVEN with the ball, press stays tiny', which was the DF3i's Press Pistol 2° geometry. The DF3i went back on Aug 10, and on the LINK's zero-lean grip that same cue is lean YOU are adding to a face with 2° to give.

That is the argument for not keeping it here at all. Two plans describing one stroke is exactly how a retired cue survives a putter change, and this one did for three days.

So: putting lives in the PUTTING LAB. The Routine plan is the whole stroke, the Setup plan is the low point and the weight, and the Distance Grind is the pace work. Nothing about putting gets written here again.
sections.k: Deliberately empty: two places describing one stroke is how a retired cue survives.

sections.t: The grip — it has its own plan now
sections.k: Deliberately empty, and the 'grip settled' line this page carried was a PUTTING verdict that outlived the section it was written for.
sections.b:
The full-swing hold lives in THE GRIP — BEFORE THE CLUB MOVES, in this lab, from Sep 9 2026. You asked for a stronger lead hand and that plan is the whole answer: how to build it, what it can and cannot do, and the gate that says whether it took.

WHY IT IS NOT WRITTEN HERE. This page carried the line 'Grip settled: conventional' in its focus from Jul 26 until Sep 9. It was true, and it was about PUTTING — conventional beat left-hand-low and the claw in the grip experiment run on the DF3i in July — and it was written in the section of this plan that used to hold the putting keys. That section moved out to the Putting lab on Aug 14. The verdict did not move with it, so a full-swing page went on saying the grip was settled and closed for six weeks, about a decision that was never about the full swing at all.

Which is the same argument the putting section below makes, from the other direction: one subject, one page. The putter's hold lives in the Putting lab's Grip & Posture plan, the full-swing hold lives in the grip plan, and neither gets a second description here. They are opposite holds anyway — the putter runs up the lifeline so the wrists cannot hinge, a full-swing club sits in the fingers so they can.

All six recordings belong to today per Jack, despite the monitor Nov 13 date. Upload order is not swing order. The late jump in the mixed 4 Iron table was 5W, not 4i improvement. Smash is club-specific: keep the wood/hybrid 1.40 threshold; no blanket iron threshold. No club read or apex below 40 ft still held for these full-swing blocks. Missing AoA/index alone is not a missing club read. Raw shots retained, history uses kept shots. Earlier mini-out/3W-in and 2i-active descriptions are superseded by current Bag; historical source notes remain.
